The fallout from Flávio Bolsonaro’s frantic flight to the US is getting messy. Not only is he facing legal jeopardy in Brazil, but his own inner circle is turning on him, the Washington Post reported.

🗣️“In response to the brutal Saudi aggression against our country and its heinous crimes…the Yemeni Armed Forces carried out six qualitative military operations using a large number of ballistic and cruise missiles and drones,” Ansar Allah-aligned Armed Forces spokesman Yahya Saree announced Saturday.
The strikes follow Friday’s Saudi attack on a market in Taiz governorate, which killed at least 30 people, and Saturday’s strike on a settlement in the outskirts of Sanaa, in which over 50 civilians, mostly children, women, and first responders were killed and wounded in a quadruple-tap [attack.](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77439)
 
The retaliatory campaign included:
 
➡️ strikes targeting King Khalid International Airport and Saudi Aramco infrastructure in Riyadh
➡️ an attack on Aramco facilities in Khurais
➡️ a strike on a pumping station in Riyadh province along the kingdom’s strategic East-West Crude Oil Pipeline
➡️ an attack on a Saudi National Guard camp in Najran near the Yemeni border (direct hit, “large number of dead and wounded,” according to Saree)
➡️ a three-phase strike targeting enemy formations in Al-Jawf province, “dozens” of enemy troops under the command of Saudi Brig. Gen. Faris Al-Shammari reported killed or injured
➡️ a strike targeting enemy forces commanded by Saudi Brig. Gen. Faris Al-Shammari in Raghwan and Madghal, Marib province
 
Saudi Arabia will be made to “pay a heavy price for every crime and act of aggression,” Saree said, warning that operations “deep inside Saudi territory” will continue based on the “siege for siege, escalation for escalation” calculus.
Houthi-aligned Supreme Political Council chairman and de-facto president Mahdi al-Mashat warned separately on Saturday that Yemen’s dead would be “avenged,” and that the Saudi “Horn of Satan” would be “punished” for its targeting of markets and civilian homes “just as the Zionist does.”

events.text:
🚀🇷🇺 Russian UAVs wipe out entire platoon of Ukrainian ground-based drones in massive bot battle
 
What may have been the biggest robot battle of the entire Russia-NATO proxy war in Ukraine just took place in northern Donetsk region, with Russian FPV and quadcopter drones deployed to stop an attack by over two dozen heavily-armed ground-based enemy bots.
The engagement between forces belonging to the 3rd Motor Rifle Division and Ukraine’s 3rd Army Corps took place on October 28, and saw the Ukrainian side attacking with:
➡️ 18 tracked robots fitted with twin Saab AT-4 RPGs
➡️ eight suicide drones strapped with explosives, presumably meant to charge enemy positions
➡️ two fitted with US-made Mk-19 automatic grenade launchers
 
Russian forces spotted the drones on approach and targeted them relentlessly using kamikaze FPV drones and bomb-dropping quadcopters, destroying the entire enemy platoon.
The make and model of the enemy equipment is unclear, although some of it looks suspiciously similar to the AI-generated tracked bots featured in ex-Ukrainian defense minister Mykhailo Fedorov’s “Army of Drones” presentation in late September. After being ousted as minister, Fedorov partnered with Palantir’s Alex Karp, promising to create [next-gen drone](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/75237) armies.
Some Russian observers pointed to the “clumsiness” of the attempted Ukrainian ground drone assault, but stressed that tanks looked similarly awkward when first deployed in the Battle of the Somme in 1916, only to emerge as war-winning technology 25 years later. Accordingly, today, the factories producing more, better and cheaper drones could decide the outcome of the wars of the future.
